title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: who can search, hold and delete organisational content, and what it costs
summary: The documented controls, commands, licensing and limits are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The page explicitly reports the conflicting Microsoft statements about premium administrator licensing, purge permissions and deletion limits.

claims.claim: The Manager assignment control is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. ... select eDiscovery Manager. ... Select Edit. ... On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> assigns a group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: Case users are added at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users > Add.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card and then select Cases in the left navigation. ... Select a case, then select Case settings. ... select Access and permissions. ... Under Users, select Add

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers adds a user or role group to a case.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/caseMembers

claims.claim: A portal path to create search permissions filters is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery search permissions filtering create filter admin portal UI New-ComplianceSecurityFilter; opened edisc-search-permission-filtering and the New-ComplianceSecurityFilter reference; read compliance-boundaries search results. Found PowerShell configuration, no portal creation path.

claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> -Action All creates the specified search permissions filter.
claims.quote: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName USDiscoveryManagers -Users "US Discovery Managers" -Filters "Mailbox_CountryCode -eq '840'" -Action All

claims.claim: Hold policy creation starts at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > Create policy.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card and then select Cases in the left navigation. ... Select a case, and then select the Hold policies tab. ... On the Hold policies dashboard, select Create policy.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/legalHolds creates a hold policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/legalHolds

claims.claim: A Purview portal deletion control for Copilot and AI application search results is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery Copilot AI data delete purge portal user interface; opened edisc-search-copilot-data and Graph purgeData reference. Results document Graph Explorer and PowerShell deletion, not a Purview portal deletion button.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseID}/searches/{ediscoverySearchID}/purgeData deletes Copilot and AI data returned by a search.
claims.quote: https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseID}/searches/{ediscoverySearchID}/purgeData

claims.claim: The premium default toggle is at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Settings > eDiscovery > General > eDiscovery (Premium).
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then go to Settings > eDiscovery > General. ... Select or clear the toggle for eDiscovery (Premium).

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell operation for the tenant-wide premium default is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery tenant default premium settings PowerShell Set policy Graph default license premium general; PowerShell ediscovery premium default Set-; Graph ediscoverySettings premium. Read edisc-settings-general and Graph API overview results; no default-setting operation.

claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions requires Organization Management membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Choose groups is an alternative to Choose users on Manage eDiscovery Manager.
claims.quote: On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Group type matters
claims.claim: Groups assigned to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup use mail-enabled security groups.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup in the eDiscovery Manager role group by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Individual users can be assigned as eDiscovery Managers.
claims.quote: Search and select the users you want to add as an eDiscovery Manager, then select Select.

claims.claim: The displayed Add-RoleGroupMember group assignment makes Managers, not Administrators.
claims.quote: However, you can't add a mail-enabled security group to the eDiscovery Administrators subgroup.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: A case can lock itself
claims.claim: Only an eDiscovery Administrator can remove case members.
claims.quote: Only an eDiscovery Administrator can remove members from a case. Users who are members of the eDiscovery Manager subgroup can't remove members from a case, even if the user created the case.

claims.claim: A user must already belong to the eDiscovery Manager role group to access and work in a case.
claims.quote: before a user can access an eDiscovery case (and perform tasks in the case), you must add the user to the eDiscovery Manager role group in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The case member request uses recipientType to specify user or roleGroup.
claims.quote: recipientType | microsoft.graph.security.recipientType | Specifies the recipient type of the eDiscovery case member. The possible values are: user, roleGroup, unknownFutureValue. Required.

claims.claim: The case member request identifies a member by id, or smtpAddress for a user, or displayName for a role group.
claims.quote: id | String | The ID of the eDiscovery case member. If not specified, then either displayName (for role group) or smtpAddress (for user) must be provided.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Configuring search permissions filters needs Organization Management and the eDiscovery administrator role.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The filter cmdlets require connections to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You need to connect to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell to use the compliance security filter cmdlets.

claims.claim: Action All applies the filter to all search actions.
claims.quote: All: The filter is applied to all search actions.

claims.claim: The legalHolds creation operation creates the hold policy rather than adding its locations.
claims.quote: Create a new ediscoveryHoldPolicy object. ... You can specify the following properties when you create an ediscoveryHoldPolicy. ... displayName ... description ... contentQuery

claims.claim: The hold policy creation request requires displayName.
claims.quote: displayName | String | The display name of the legal hold policy. Required.

claims.claim: The hold policy creation request optionally sets contentQuery.
claims.quote: contentQuery | String | KQL query that specifies content to be held in the specified locations. Optional.

claims.claim: Mailbox sources are added to the created hold policy separately.
claims.quote: POST /security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/legalHolds/{ediscoveryHoldPolicyId}/userSources

claims.claim: Site sources are added to the created hold policy separately.
claims.quote: POST /security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/legalHolds/{ediscoveryHoldPolicyId}/siteSources

claims.claim: Deleting AI activity data requires Search And Purge.
claims.quote: To delete AI activity data, you need to be assigned the Search And Purge role.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Risks and limits: Deleting Copilot data
claims.claim: Holds and retention policies on the target mailbox must be removed before deleting Copilot data or the data is retained.
claims.quote: Before you can delete Copilot or other AI application data from a mailbox, you have to remove any hold or retention policy that is assigned to a target mailbox. If you don't remove the hold or retention policy, the data you're trying to delete is retained.

claims.claim: purgeAreas can select mailboxes as the purge location type.
claims.quote: purgeAreas | microsoft.graph.security.purgeAreas | Option to define the locations to be in scope of the purge action. The possible values are: mailboxes, teamsMessages, unknownFutureValue.

claims.claim: purgeType can select recoverable or permanentlyDelete.
claims.quote: purgeType | microsoft.graph.security.purgeType | Options that control whether the action is soft delete or hard delete. The possible values are: recoverable, unknownFutureValue, permanentlyDelete.

claims.claim: Only eDiscovery Administrators can access the premium default setting.
claims.quote: Only users assigned to the eDiscovery Administrators role can access this setting.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The premium default affects new cases only.
claims.quote: Enabling premium eDiscovery features only affects new cases and doesn't affect the license state of any existing cases.

claims.claim: The premium default setting is unavailable with Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3.
claims.quote: This setting isn't available for organizations with Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 subscription.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The premium default can be overridden for an individual case.
claims.quote: You can override this setting on a per-case basis after creating a new case in the settings for a case.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery identifies, preserves, reviews and exports Microsoft 365 content for investigations and legal cases.
claims.quote: Use Microsoft Purview eDiscovery to identify, review, and manage content in Microsoft 365 services to support your investigations. ... Use eDiscovery cases to identify, hold, and export content found in mailboxes and sites.

claims.claim: A case contains the searches, holds and review sets related to a specific investigation.
claims.quote: An eDiscovery case contains all searches, holds, and review sets related to a specific investigation.

claims.claim: Each case has membership that controls access to the case and its contents.
claims.quote: You can also assign members to a case to control who can access the case and view the contents of the case.

claims.claim: A search can cover Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups and Viva Engage together.
claims.quote: Search for content that's stored in Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, SharePoint sites, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups, and Viva Engage Teams. ... You can search mailboxes and sites in the same eDiscovery search

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions are stored as individual items in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Each Microsoft 365 Copilot interaction is stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox as an individual message-class item

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions can be searched with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: When these items appear in eDiscovery search results, review sets, or exports (PST files, individual messages, or Microsoft Graph)

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions can be held with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: eDiscovery content search, legal hold, export search results for Copilot interactions | Included | Included | Included | Not included | Included

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions can be exported with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: When these items appear in eDiscovery search results, review sets, or exports (PST files, individual messages, or Microsoft Graph)

claims.claim: Microsoft retired classic eDiscovery experiences on 31 August 2025.
claims.quote: Microsoft retired all classic eDiscovery experiences on August 31, 2025.

claims.claim: Search finds content using keyword queries and conditions.
claims.quote: Create Keyword Query Language (KeyQL) search queries to search for content keywords that match query criteria. You can also include conditions to narrow the scope of your search.

claims.claim: Search shows statistics and samples.
claims.quote: After you run a search, you can view statistics of the estimated search results ... You can also view a representative sample of the items included in the search results.

claims.where: What it is: The parts; Why it matters
claims.claim: A case hold preserves content in selected mailboxes and sites until the hold is released.
claims.quote: When you place content locations on hold, you preserve content until you remove the content location from the hold or until you delete or release the hold.

claims.claim: Export copies results from their original locations into a downloadable package.
claims.quote: When you export search results, items are copied from their original content location and packaged. Then you can download those items in the export package to a local computer.

claims.claim: A review set holds copied items in a Microsoft-provided Azure Storage location.
claims.quote: A review set is a secure, Microsoft-provided Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud. When you add data to a review set, the collected items are copied from their original content location to the review set.

claims.claim: Items in a review set can be filtered, tagged and analysed.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Search and delete can remove harmful or high-risk email.
claims.quote: Use eDiscovery to search for and delete email messages, Microsoft Teams chat messages, and Copilot and AI application data across your organization. This capability helps you find and remove content that's potentially harmful or high-risk.

claims.claim: Search and delete can remove Teams chat messages.
claims.quote: Use eDiscovery to search for and delete email messages, Microsoft Teams chat messages, and Copilot and AI application data across your organization.

claims.claim: Search and delete can remove Copilot and AI application data.
claims.quote: Use eDiscovery to search for and delete email messages, Microsoft Teams chat messages, and Copilot and AI application data across your organization.

claims.claim: Review sets are premium eDiscovery features.
claims.quote: | Review sets |  | Supported. |

claims.claim: Analytics are premium eDiscovery features.
claims.quote: | Analytics |  | Supported. |

claims.claim: Tagging is a premium eDiscovery feature.
claims.quote: | Tagging |  | Supported. |

claims.claim: Decryption is a premium eDiscovery feature.
claims.quote: | Decryption |  | Supported. |

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Role-group membership controls which eDiscovery tasks a person can perform.
claims.quote: Use role-based access control (RBAC) permissions to control what eDiscovery-related tasks that different users can perform. You can use a built-in eDiscovery-related role group or create custom role groups that assign specific eDiscovery permissions.

claims.claim: Search permissions filters build compliance boundaries limiting which mailboxes and sites an eDiscovery manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to create logical boundaries (called compliance boundaries) within an organization that control the user content locations (such as mailboxes, SharePoint sites, and OneDrive accounts) that specific eDiscovery managers can search.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs administrators to retention policies and labels for long-term retention unrelated to investigations.
claims.quote: For long term data retention not related to eDiscovery investigations, use retention policies and retention labels.

claims.claim: eDiscovery searches include content generated by other Microsoft 365 apps that store data in mailboxes and sites.
claims.quote: Searches include content generated by other Microsoft 365 apps that store data in mailboxes and sites.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.* as an item class for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.
claims.quote: | Microsoft 365 Copilot | IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.Copilot.* |

claims.quote:
| eDiscovery (standard) for sites and files | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: The table includes premium eDiscovery for E5-level plans, Microsoft Purview Suite and the Microsoft 365 E5 eDiscovery & Audit add-on.
claims.quote: | eDiscovery (premium) | Included | Not included | Included | Included | Not included |

claims.claim: Compliance boundaries have no separate licensing requirement beyond applicable eDiscovery licensing.
claims.quote: Compliance boundaries are an eDiscovery configuration capability for limiting which content locations and cases eDiscovery managers can access, and don't have separate licensing requirements beyond applicable eDiscovery licensing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Holds; What to check
claims.claim: Each user whose content is preserved needs an eligible hold licence.
claims.quote: eDiscovery holds require an eligible license on every user whose content you preserve.

claims.claim: Office 365 F1 and F3 do not include rights to be the target of an eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: Frontline subscriptions such as Office 365 F1 and F3 don't include the rights required to be the target of an eDiscovery hold.

claims.claim: A shared mailbox on hold needs Exchange Online Plan 2 or Plan 1 with the Exchange Online Archiving add-on.
claims.quote: Placing a shared mailbox on hold using Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (standard or premium) is subject to the same licensing requirements as placing a hold directly in Exchange Online—Exchange Online Plan 2 or Exchange Online Plan 1 with the Exchange Online Archiving add-on.

claims.claim: The permissions page requires an E5 licence or an eligible add-on for the user whose data is analysed with premium features.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Premium analysis; Open questions
claims.claim: The permissions page says administrators assigned to cases do not need an E5 licence to collect, view and analyse with premium features.
claims.quote: Administrators, compliance officers, or legal personnel who are assigned to cases as members and use premium eDiscovery features to collect, view, and analyze data don't need an E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Premium analysis; Open questions
claims.claim: The service description instead requires the appropriate licence or add-on for both the analysed user and the analysing administrator.
claims.quote: When eDiscovery (premium) features are used, both the user whose data is being analyzed and the administrator performing the analysis must have the appropriate license or add-on.

claims.claim: Storage for Microsoft 365 data is included in the enterprise subscription.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 data: Non-AI data from Microsoft 365 services and applications. ... This data storage is included in your enterprise subscription and isn't subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Storage for Microsoft 365 AI data is included in the enterprise subscription.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 AI data: AI data from Microsoft 365 services and applications. ... This data storage is included in your enterprise subscription and isn't subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft 365 AI data storage is subject to pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: This data storage isn't included in your enterprise subscription and is subject to pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Non-Microsoft 365 AI data includes Copilot in Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot and connected AI applications.
claims.quote: This data type includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, and any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.claim: Direct portal exports of non-Microsoft 365 AI data are within pay-as-you-go storage billing scope.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data: ... Direct export of this data from cases by using the Microsoft Purview portal

claims.claim: Adding non-Microsoft 365 AI data to review sets is within pay-as-you-go storage billing scope.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data: ... Adding this data to a review set

claims.claim: Graph exports of non-Microsoft 365 AI data are within pay-as-you-go storage billing scope.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data: ... Exporting this data by using Microsoft Graph API

claims.claim: Search processes do not incur the non-Microsoft 365 AI data pay-as-you-go charge.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes don't use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data and are included in your enterprise subscription: ... All search processes

claims.claim: Hold processes do not incur the non-Microsoft 365 AI data pay-as-you-go charge.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes don't use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data and are included in your enterprise subscription: ... All hold processes

claims.claim: Case management processes do not incur the non-Microsoft 365 AI data pay-as-you-go charge.
claims.quote: The following eDiscovery processes don't use pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data and are included in your enterprise subscription: ... All case management processes

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview pricing page publishes the per-GB storage rate rather than the eDiscovery billing page.
claims.quote: This functionality is billed based on the amount of data processed and stored through export and review set each month, equivalent to $20 per GB per month.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Graph APIs with E3
claims.claim: Using Microsoft Graph APIs with E3 eDiscovery licensing requires an Azure subscription configured for pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Before you can ... use Microsoft Graph APIs with an E3 eDiscovery license, you must configure an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Graph APIs with E3
claims.claim: Microsoft currently excludes API usage other than Export APIs from billing.
claims.quote: Currently, usage of all APIs except Export APIs doesn't contribute towards billing.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Graph APIs with E3
claims.claim: E3 Export API billing is based on exported volume above an included monthly free amount.
claims.quote: Usage of Export API is billed based on the volume of data exported. Each organization receives an included amount of free storage per month, with additional usage billed at a set price per GB.

claims.where: Risks and limits: eDiscovery Administrators see every case
claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators can access all cases and all case data.
claims.quote: Access all cases that are listed on the eDiscovery area in the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Access case data for any case in the organization.

claims.where: Risks and limits: eDiscovery Administrators see every case; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft advises limiting the number of eDiscovery Administrators.
claims.quote: because eDiscovery Administrators can access potentially sensitive information in the results of a compliance search, you should limit the number of people who are eDiscovery Administrators.

claims.where: Risks and limits: eDiscovery Administrators see every case
claims.claim: The permissions page says eDiscovery Managers can access and manage only the cases they create.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.

claims.where: Risks and limits: eDiscovery Administrators see every case
claims.claim: The permissions page also says non-Administrator users see only cases where they are members.
claims.quote: For users who aren't eDiscovery Administrators, the cases shown are limited to those where the user is a member.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A case can lock itself; What to check
claims.claim: If a case's only member leaves, an eDiscovery Administrator is needed to regain access.
claims.quote: If a person who is the only member of an eDiscovery case leaves your organization, no one ... can access that eDiscovery case ... But because an eDiscovery Administrator can access all eDiscovery cases in the organization, they can view the case

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role-group edits silently change case access
claims.claim: Adding or removing a role from a role group that belongs to cases removes the group from those cases.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group type matters
claims.claim: Exchange distribution groups and Microsoft 365 Groups are unsupported for assignment to the Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: Exchange distribution groups and Microsoft 365 Groups aren't supported. You must use a mail-enabled security group

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group type matters
claims.claim: A mail-enabled security group cannot be a case member.
claims.quote: You also can't add a mail-enabled security group as a member of a case.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Holds are snapshots and take time
claims.claim: Group membership is captured as a point-in-time snapshot when a hold policy is created.
claims.quote: Group membership is captured as a point-in-time snapshot when the hold policy is created. This applies to every supported group type

claims.where: Risks and limits: Holds are snapshots and take time
claims.claim: Members added to a group after hold creation are not automatically placed on hold.
claims.quote: Members added to the group later are not automatically placed on hold; members removed from the group remain on hold until you update or release the policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Holds are snapshots and take time
claims.claim: An eDiscovery hold can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: After you create an eDiscovery hold, it might take up to 24 hours for the hold to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Holds are snapshots and take time
claims.claim: SharePoint Recycle Bin content is not indexed.
claims.quote: The Recycle Bin in SharePoint sites isn't indexed and therefore unavailable for searching. As a result, eDiscovery searches can't find any Recycle Bin content to place holds.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Holds are snapshots and take time
claims.claim: Selecting a subsite for a hold places the hold on the parent SharePoint site.
claims.quote: If you select a subsite, the hold is placed on the parent SharePoint site instead.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Filters have a ceiling

claims.where: Risks and limits: Filters have a ceiling

claims.quote: Search permissions filtering can't be used to limit who can search public folders in Exchange.
